newsitem.title: FRANCE: Thomson Multimedia no comment on reported '96 loss.
newsitem.headline: Thomson Multimedia no comment on reported '96 loss.

text.p: French consumer electronics firm Thomson Multimedia (TMM) declined comment on Thursday on a newspaper report it would post a net attributable loss of three billion francs for 1996.

"I am not confirming these figures. The 1996 accounts have not been closed," a TMM spokesman said, commenting on newspaper Les Echos which reported the expected net loss for the year and an operating loss of 500 million francs.
TMM is part of the Thomson SA group, which is being privatised by the government in two parts. The defence electronics arm Thomson-CSF will be sold first.
TMM lost 1.09 billion francs in 1995. It reported a net loss of three billion and a one billion operating loss for the first half of 1996.
The spokesman recalled comments by chairman Alain Prestat who said at the end of October that the second half would see a large positive operating profit and perhaps break even of the net result.
TMM is reorganising its activities, having taken a 1.2 billion franc charge in the first half, to return to profit.
Industry Minister Franck Borotra said on Wednesday TMM would get a capital injection in the next few weeks.
This recapitalisation, estimated at 10 billion francs, will cut financing costs by 600 million francs.
TMM expects to be structurally profitable in 1998 when it will receive payments on patents of its GE/RCA U.S. unit under the terms of the original acquisition deal with General Electric .
